claim: A: the street radar (60 GHz, module range 20 m) reaches the dry road 4.6 m below the lens and the water surface in between
law: Free-space propagation of a 60 GHz pulse; module range 20 m (Acconeer product page, as cited in FLG-PRB-001, 2026-09-25)

claim: A: street depth error stays within 10 mm when the radar module is accurate to 2 mm (assumed) and datum, pole expansion and ripple add 5, 2 and 3 mm
law: Root sum square of independent errors; the 2 mm module accuracy is assumed (S3), so the budget holds only if the module meets it
check: 2 mm <= 7.88 mm: the module may be as poor as 7.9 mm before the 10 mm limit is reached, but pole bow in the sun (about 3 mm for a 5 K difference across the pole, independent review) and the worst-case sum of 12 mm are not inside the RSS

claim: A: a 60 GHz carrier (wavelength 5.00 mm) gives a 2 mm range accuracy
law: Coherent radar reads range from the phase of the echo: a 1 mm change in range shifts the phase by 4 pi / lambda = 2.52 rad, so 2 mm is several radians of phase
check: Phase argument supports mm-level accuracy, but the module's guaranteed accuracy, beam width through the PTFE lens and curb echo rejection are not in a data sheet yet

claim: A: speed of sound c = 331.3 + 0.606 T (m/s) used to compensate the drain ranger over -20 to 50 C
law: Ideal gas: c = sqrt(gamma R T / M) with gamma 1.4, R 287.05 J/(kg K); worst deviation 0.34 % over the range
check: claimed 361.6 m/s at 50 C, estimate 360 m/s at 50 C (ratio 1.00)

claim: A: drain level error stays within 20 mm at the 950 mm maximum range, with the NTC correcting air temperature to 2 K (10 mm module accuracy, 3 mm datum)
law: Two-way time of flight, c = 331.3 + 0.606 T; root sum square of module, temperature and datum errors (an uncompensated 10 K swing would add 16.8 mm); if the module accuracy is plus or minus (1 cm + 0.3 % of range) the error is about 13.6 mm, and humidity in a saturated basin adds a further 0.3 to 1 % to c, both to check on the data sheet

claim: A: the ultrasonic ranger (60 degree beam) reads the water surface 0.3 m to 1.25 m below it inside a 69 mm bore tube
law: The axial echo off the water is the shortest path for a smooth wall; but slot edges, joints, the cable loop and drops inside the tube can return an echo before the water echo, so the first echo is not always the water
check: Smooth-wall geometry supports it; echoes from the slot edges, the cable loop and condensation on the face are not excluded by the module (independent review), so the wet probe and a recorded empty-tube background are needed

claim: A: the slotted stilling tube follows a basin rising at 10 mm/s with a lag head under 5 mm even with only the lowest slot row wet
law: Orifice flow, v = Q / (Cd A) with Cd 0.6, head = v^2 / 2 g

claim: A: the 40 x 40 x 1.6 mm aluminium arm survives a 50 kg person hanging on the head (misuse case)
law: Cantilever to the top brace pin, sigma = M / Z; 6063-T6 class yield 214 MPa (typical, assumed)

claim: A: the 25 x 25 x 1.6 mm knee brace and its pins carry the same load
law: L/r = 37 is below the Euler range, so Johnson inelastic buckling (28533 N) and pin bearing in 1.6 mm walls (11520 N) apply; the Euler value (73 kN) is not valid

claim: A: two band clamps alone hold the arm against the twist of a 35 m/s wind along the street (60 mm pole; on a 40 mm pole friction gives 24.0 N m)
law: Coulomb friction, mu 0.30, 1 kN preload per band (FieldNode assumption); wind drag, q = 0.5 rho v^2
closed_by: S11 carries the twist as a second path; on a 40 mm pole it is the only one

claim: A: the M8 A4-80 anti-rotation through-bolt holds the arm against the same twist
law: The bolt bends as a 21.7 mm cantilever out of the pole wall through the spacer (independent review corrected the first couple model): M = f_y Z, f_y 600 MPa (A4-80), stress-area section; plate load 52 mm from the pole axis
closed_by: FLG-CAL-001 H2b; FLG-DDR-004 F2 (class raised from A4-70 to A4-80)

claim: A: the added mass on the pole stays at or under 5 kg
law: Sum of part volumes times density from the CAD model plus FieldNode 2.45 kg and cables (FLG-CAL-001 I1, I2)
closed_by: weigh at TRL 4; FLG-DEC-001 item 3 (bracket plate to 2.5 mm)

claim: A: pole expansion moves the lens by about 2 mm over a 35 K swing
law: Linear expansion, dL = alpha L dT with steel alpha 12e-6 per K

claim: A: stored energy runs the sensors for 5 days without sun at event sampling
law: Usable 15.36 Wh (FND-CAL-001), draw from the sampling cycle energy of FLG-CAL-001 D1 to D4; days at -20 C used

claim: A: normal-mode uplinks (every 15 min, 20-byte payload, SF9) stay within The Things Network fair use of 30 s airtime per day
law: LoRa time on air (Semtech formula); fair use 30 s/day (The Things Network, checked 2026-10-31)
closed_by: FLG-CAL-001 E1; PR-007 stays at risk at SF10 and slower

claim: A: event-mode uplinks every 60 s at SF9 stay within the EU868 1 % duty cycle
law: Duty cycle = time on air / interval; limit 1 % (EU868 sub-band, ETSI EN 300 220; text not reopened, see FLG-REG-001)

claim: A: the drain head face, 0.9 m under water in the worst design flood, stays inside the 1 m rating of its IP67 module
law: Hydrostatic head p = rho g h; IP67 is 1 m for 30 min (IEC 60529)
closed_by: PR-009 stays at risk: 72 h duration unverified (FLG-CAL-001 K1)

claim: A: the drain head survives 72 h under silty stormwater at 2 m (IP68)
law: IP68 is defined by agreement with the maker, not by the code; the potted electronics are sealed but the transducer face keeps the stock IP67 seal
check: Not shown by calculation; needs the module maker's rating or an immersion test at TRL 4. Pressure at 2 m is 19.6 kPa

claim: A: stainless A4 fasteners in a 6063 aluminium arm and bracket survive road-salt spray for the life of the pilot
law: Galvanic couple of stainless steel and aluminium; the cathode (fastener) is small and the anode (aluminium) large, the favourable area ratio, and anodising or sleeves separate them
check: Favourable area ratio and crush sleeves; chloride splash can still pit the aluminium at the contact, to confirm with a coating or an isolating washer at TRL 3

claim: A: the PVC stilling tube stays below its service temperature in a shaded basin
law: PVC-U typical maximum continuous service temperature 60 C (manufacturer data, to confirm for the chosen pipe); PVC-U also turns brittle in the cold, so impacts at -20 C are a handling risk

claim: A: 5 x 50 mm slots in the stilling tube stay open in silty, leaf-laden stormwater for a season
law: Slots 5 mm wide pass silt but clog with leaf litter and biofilm over weeks in warm standing water; 40 slots in 10 rows leave 75 % of the open area if a quarter clog
check: Open area is 10000 mm2 against a 3739 mm2 bore, so a quarter clogged still passes the flow of S7; cleaning interval to assess

claim: A: an event-mode alert reaches the service within 120 s at SF10 on a private gateway, worst case without a lost packet (10 s sample, two confirming samples, wake, airtime, duty-cycle wait, 4.7 s network)
law: Sum of the delays; SF11 gives about 134 s and SF12 about 217 s, so PR-006 holds to SF10 only (independent review)

claim: A: the street head's I2C bus stays within 400 pF on a 3 m cable
law: Bus capacitance = cable length x pF/m + 50 pF: 350 pF at an assumed 100 pF/m; a 150 pF/m cable gives 500 pF
check: Passes at the assumed cable; the real cable's capacitance is on its data sheet

claim: B: a 0 to 20 kPa vented transducer covers 600 mm in the street (5.9 kPa) and the 1.25 m basin range (12.3 kPa)
law: Hydrostatic pressure p = rho g h, gauge pressure against the vented atmosphere

claim: B: street depth error stays within 10 mm (0.25 % of a 20 kPa range, 0 to 40 C water density, 5 g/l silt, 5 mm datum)
law: Root sum square; water density 999.8 to 992.2 kg/m3; silt density rise = SSC (1 - rho_w / rho_s), rho_s 2.65; accuracy class assumed

claim: B: the vented cable keeps the atmospheric reference dry for years
law: A vented gauge transducer breathes through its cable; condensation or water in the vent tube shifts the zero
check: Desiccant or a PTFE vent membrane is the usual remedy; lifetime in a flooded basin is not shown

claim: B: a stand pipe on the curb face does not split or crush the transducer when street water freezes at -20 C
law: Water expands about 9 % on freezing and can split a closed pipe; the bottom cap has four drain holes, so only a film freezes
check: Drain holes leave no standing column after an event; a trapped film is expected to be harmless, to confirm

claim: C: the street float (hollow shell, 42 mm OD) floats with its magnet at under 70 % of its volume submerged
law: Archimedes: weight (shell 29.2 g, plus about 3 g of foam) = displaced water; solid ring first pass was 44.4 g against 33.7 g of buoyancy and sank; the voids are filled with closed-cell foam (about 3 g) so a leaking shell still floats (FLG-DDR-004 F1)
check: 61 % of buoyancy used <= 70 % of buoyancy used

claim: C: the basin float (hollow shell, 56 mm OD) floats with its magnet at under 70 % of its volume submerged
law: Archimedes: weight (shell 47.0 g, plus about 3 g of foam) = displaced water; solid ring first pass was 106.5 g against 97.4 g and sank
check: 48 % of buoyancy used <= 70 % of buoyancy used

claim: C: a reed chain at 25 mm pitch reads the level to 25 mm steps (plus or minus 12.5 mm)
law: Resolution of a switch chain = pitch; the level is the highest closed reed, with one or two reeds closing at once, so the error is at most one pitch
check: True as stated. It exceeds the 10 mm street target of PR-002, so this is scored against the user requirements in FLG-OPT-001, not a failure of the science

claim: C: a ring magnet beside the sealed stem closes a glass reed switch 1.9 mm from the stem axis
law: Reed switches close at 10 to 30 ampere-turns of applied field; a sintered ring magnet at a few millimetres gives a field far above that; hysteresis spreads the closing height by a few mm
check: Plausible; the closing height and its spread need the reed's data sheet, assumed typical 10 to 30 AT

claim: C: the floats move freely on 16 mm stems in silty stormwater and at -20 C
law: Silt and biofilm in the 0.9 mm radial gap between bore and stem can bind a float; ice binds it solid in a frozen tube
check: Plausible; the bottom cap drain holes empty the street pipe, the basin float is not protected from ice, to assess in OPT scoring
